title: Test fit against the official scope
statement: Test a question's fit to the curriculum by checking that the unit's official scope can answer it.
detail: A study summarised in the AP question work measured validity partly with a question-answering test, on the view that a curriculum-aligned question should be answerable using the curriculum's own scope definition, alongside similarity to the official curriculum (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`). With that yardstick, grounding generation in official curriculum documents took validity from 12-15% to 92-96% with the same generator. That result is about grounding, so it shows the test in use, not that the test is valid.
against: The test's own accuracy is not reported; it was the yardstick, not the thing tested. The study covers one other subject, secondary mathematics (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`, line 276).

evidence.quote: **How validity is measured:** Semantic Textual Similarity against official curriculum + RAG-QA test (a curriculum-aligned question should be answerable using the curriculum's own scope definition). This is analogous to our curriculum_alignment dimension.

RAG methods go from 12-15% validity to 92-96% validity by grounding generation in official curriculum documents. The study uses GPT-4o as the generator for all conditions — the variable is retrieval, not the model.

citations.ref: Automated Generation of Curriculum-Aligned MCQs for Malaysian Secondary Mathematics (arXiv:2508.04442)
